end.summary:
Recognised triangles and polygons in different positions and sizes, using straight sides, corners, and a closed shape.
Described triangles by equal sides and by angles; this was shown on new examples.
Named polygons by side count, including pentagon and hexagon; some names still need checking next time.
Explored that turning or changing side lengths does not change a polygon’s name.
end.parentNote: Veer practised identifying triangles and polygons by counting straight sides and corners, and describing triangles by equal sides and angle types. They used useful reasons such as a closed shape having six straight sides, and recognised equilateral, right-angled, and isosceles triangles. Polygon names by side count were not steady across all examples, so please practise naming shapes from 3 to 8 sides at home by counting the sides aloud.
